answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake, then slash it when independent peers prove that it double-voted or fabricated a task result. Votes count only from staked identities, and a challenge window lets honest agents submit verifiable evidence before rewards settle. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock up real capital for every identity and risk losing it; copying keys is cheap, but buying influence is not. Even a wander toward the summit of influence must follow the same costly vine of collateral and accountability.
